name: allocArray
title: Allocates an empty vector, matrix or array

origin.description: Allocates an array filled with one value, faster than the corresponding function in R.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: An integer vector of length at least one giving the array dimensions. It is coerced with as.integer. The first element varies fastest.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A single integer, numeric, or logical value copied into every element. The result uses that storage mode. The default 0 is double.

origin.details: The installed function returns an array of the same mode as value. A length-two dim is a matrix. A negative product of the dimensions is "negative length vectors are not allowed". A positive product that still contains a negative dimension is "the dims contain negative values", and a missing dimension on that path is "the dims contain missing values".
origin.value: An array with the given dimensions and the storage mode of value.

translation.description: Allocates an array filled with one value.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Dimension vector of length at least one. This is dim in R, not the dim. argument used by other matrixStats functions. dim_ is accepted as an alias when dim is omitted. Coerced like R as.integer. Axis 0 is the first dimension. A length-two dim is a matrix, with axis 0 as rows and axis 1 as columns.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: One value copied into every element. A float is double, an int is integer, and a bool is logical. None is R's bare NA, which is logical. Integer NA is -2147483648. Double NA is nan. The default 0.0 is double.

translation.details: The fill lives in the Rust crate allocmatrix, ported from matrixStats src/allocMatrix2.c. Dimensions are multiplied in float64, matching the C product. A negative product is "negative length vectors are not allowed", and that is reported before the value's type is checked. A positive product that still contains a negative dimension is "the dims contain negative values" after the type check. A missing dimension on that path is "the dims contain missing values". A product above 2^52 is "vector is too large". Logical values are stored as int32: 1, 0, and -2147483648 for NA. Extra arguments are ignored.
translation.value: A NumPy array whose shape is dim. float64 for a double value, int32 for an integer or logical value.
translation.example:
from matrixstats.alloc import allocArray

allocArray((2, 3), True)
